topic: Looking up a company's phone number yourself before calling back, instead of using a number given in a suspicious call or text
headline: Call Back The Safe Way
supporting_text: Skip numbers from texts or voicemails. Search the company's official number yourself first.
caption:
⚡ TODAY’S 30-SECOND TECH WIN

Getting a call or text that says there's a problem with your bank or account can feel urgent.

Scammers count on that urgency, and they often leave a phone number for you to call back.

Instead of using that number, hang up, take a breath, and look up the company's real number yourself through their official website or the back of your card.

Then call that number directly if you want to check on anything.

This one small pause can help you avoid talking to someone pretending to be your bank.

Save this tip for later.

Follow @DigitalCalmDaily for one simple 30-Second Tech Win every day.
visual_symbol: a phone with a magnifying glass over a number pad
reel_hook: Stop scam calls with one pause
reel_steps: Hang up calmly, don't call the number given
Search the company's real number online or on your card
Call that number yourself to check the issue
